title: Parametric amplification in a Kerr Oscillator based on Ne FIB Nanobridges
authors: Parth Bhandari, Laith Meti, Gemma Chapman, Edward Romans, John Gallop, Ling Hao
abstract: Superconducting circuits play a crucial role in the advancement of quantum computing and quantum sensing. Typically such circuits require the presence of a non-linear element, where the engineered anharmonicity (Kerr factor) and resonant linewidth determine the potential applications of the circuit. In this work we have fabricated Nb-based CPW resonators embedded with a DC SQUID incorporating Nb nanobridges as the weak links. We use two-tone spectroscopy to study the non-linear behaviour of the device at 15 mK up to a field of 2.48 mT. Under the application of a blue-detuned pump, the device shows a decrease in the resonant frequency which is used to estimate the Kerr factor. We further apply a red-detuned pump to go beyond the bifurcation threshold and observe the appearance of an additional idler mode with net gain. The gain of the device was maximized by further decreasing the pump frequency, showing a maximum amplification of 15 dB. Finally, we show agreement between the Kerr non-linear oscillator model and the measured transmission spectrum, and highlight further design modifications to improve the gain and bandwidth of such devices.
summary: This paper reports on the experimental demonstration of parametric amplification in a superconducting Kerr Oscillator built using Nb nanobridges. By employing two-tone spectroscopy, the authors characterized the non-linear response and achieved a maximum gain of 15 dB. This work validates the use of such superconducting circuits for advanced quantum sensing and readout applications.
main_problem: The paper investigates the feasibility and performance of parametric amplification within a Kerr Oscillator circuit, a key component for quantum sensing and readout.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated parametric gain up to 15 dB using a superconducting circuit containing Nb nanobridges, confirming the model's predictions.
method: The study combines two-tone spectroscopy measurements with theoretical modeling based on the driven Kerr nonlinear oscillator equation of motion.
model_or_system: The physical system is an Nb-based CPW resonator embedded with a DC SQUID containing Nb nanobridges. The dynamics are modeled by a Kerr oscillator Hamiltonian and its corresponding equation of motion.
key_observables: Maximum amplification (15 dB), Kerr factor (K), resonant frequency, and the appearance of an idler mode.
important_parameters: Operating temperature (15 mK), magnetic field tolerance (up to 2.48 mT), and the ratio of Kerr nonlinearity to linewidth (|K|/$\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the weakly nonlinear regime ($|K|/\kappa < 1$) and that the feedline supports bidirectional propagation for the EOM derivation.
figures_summary: Figures show the resonator transmission spectrum fitted to extract parameters, and spectral evolution plots demonstrating the gain profile as the pump frequency is swept.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using the Kerr oscillator model, then details the experimental measurement techniques (two-tone spectroscopy) to estimate the Kerr factor, and finally demonstrates parametric gain by sweeping the pump frequency.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering of non-linear elements in superconducting circuits, which is fundamental for building quantum transducers, quantum memories, and high-sensitivity quantum sensors.
